issues.t: S-10 Blazer: automatic transmission slips or loses gears
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring RPM between shifts, harsh or late shifts, or suddenly no 2nd, 4th or reverse. The fluid may smell burnt.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic (4L60-E) wears its 3-4 clutches, and an internal part called the sun shell can crack, taking out several gears. Owners report failures around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. If it slips or loses gears, avoid towing and get a transmission shop diagnosis; a rebuild with upgraded parts is the usual fix.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, the engine runs hot, the oil turns milky, or you smell coolant after driving.
issues.why: The original intake manifold gaskets on the 4.3L V6 break down with heat and age and leak coolant outside or into the engine.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. If it keeps dropping or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the gaskets replaced before the engine bearings are damaged.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: central "spider" fuel injector sticks or leaks
issues.sym: Rough running right after a cold start, long cranking, misfires and a check engine light, often worse after sitting overnight.
issues.why: The 4.3L uses one central injector unit with small poppet valves feeding each cylinder. Deposits make them stick, and the unit can leak fuel into the intake.
issues.next: Have misfire codes and fuel pressure checked. Replacing the central injector unit is the usual repair.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Cranks but won't start, stalls or sputters, or loses power going up hills.
issues.why: The electric pump in the fuel tank wears out or develops an electrical fault. Owners of 2000 models report it around 85,000 miles.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested. A failed pump means replacing the pump module inside the tank.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge bounces, sticks at half, or shows fuel left when the tank is nearly empty.
issues.why: The fuel level sender (a float on the pump module inside the tank) wears out.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until it's fixed so you don't run dry. The fix is a new sender or pump module.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: lower ball joints wear out
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints on this platform wear early, especially on 4WD models, and a badly worn joint can separate.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked for play at each tire rotation once past 50,000 miles, and replace them as soon as they're worn.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: upper ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front end. If the joint separates, steering control can be lost and the suspension can collapse.
issues.why: Corrosion can wear out the front upper ball joints on these models. GM recalled them to replace the upper control arms or joints.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If the front end clunks, have it inspected before driving at speed.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: gauges stop working
issues.sym: The speedometer, fuel, temperature or tach gauges stop moving or drop to zero, sometimes along with the radio.
issues.why: The gauge motors and solder joints inside the cluster fail, or loose connections cut power to it.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the cluster tested. Repair shops can rebuild it or replace the gauge motors.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: ABS light on from failed brake control module
issues.sym: The ABS warning light stays on. Normal brakes work, but anti-lock braking is switched off.
issues.why: The electronic brake control module on the ABS unit fails, or a wheel speed sensor goes bad.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read to find the faulty part. The brakes still stop the truck, but drive carefully on slick roads until it's fixed.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: blower works only on some speeds
issues.sym: The heater and A/C fan works only on high, or quits on some speeds.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor burns out. A worn blower motor can overload it.
issues.next: Replace the resistor. If the fan motor is noisy or slow, replace it too.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: doors sag from worn hinge pins
issues.sym: Doors drop when opened and must be lifted to close, or they creak and pop.
issues.why: The hinge pins and bushings wear out, especially on the heavy front doors.
issues.next: Install a hinge pin and bushing kit before the worn hinge damages the door or striker.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: oil pressure gauge drops or jumps
issues.sym: The oil pressure gauge falls to zero or swings while the engine sounds normal.
issues.why: The oil pressure sender on the 4.3L V6 often fails. Real low pressure must still be ruled out.
issues.next: Check the oil level, then have pressure checked with a mechanical gauge. If pressure is good, a new sender fixes it.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: misfire from distributor cap and rotor
issues.sym: Misfires, rough idle, hard starting and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: The plastic distributor cap on the 4.3L V6 sits in a hot spot, warps and wears the rotor.
issues.next: Replace the cap, rotor and plug wires as a set; it's a simple first fix for misfires.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: brake lights and hazards can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights or rear hazard lights don't come on.
issues.why: The turn signal and hazard (multifunction) switch can fail open, cutting power to the brake and rear hazard lights. GM recalled it twice.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Have someone check your brake lights; drive with care until fixed.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: windshield wipers work on and off (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop or work only some of the time.
issues.why: Cracked solder joints on the wiper control board cut power to the wipers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; a dealer fixes it free.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: seat belt webbing may separate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. A belt could tear in a second impact or rollover.
issues.why: Outboard seat belt webbing could be damaged and separate in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the belts inspected.

issues.t: S-10 Blazer: rear brake pipe or control arm nuts (recalls)
issues.sym: A brake fluid leak near the rear axle, a soft pedal, or clunking from the front suspension.
issues.why: On some 1998 models a rear brake pipe could crack from fatigue, and on others the right lower control arm nuts were not tightened enough.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer inspect both items.

issues.t: Crossover: transmission shudder or harsh shifts
issues.sym: A shake or shudder at low to moderate speeds, or harsh, slipping or flaring shifts at low miles.
issues.why: GM has issued several service bulletins for the 9-speed automatic, including a torque converter clutch shudder fixed with a fluid drain and refill, and relearn procedures for harsh shifts.
issues.next: Tell the dealer exactly when it happens. Ask whether bulletins PIP5608H, 16NA019 or 23-NA-072 apply; many cases are fixed with a fluid service or software relearn.

issues.t: Crossover: transmission fluid leak from missing bolts (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid drips under the front of the SUV. If enough is lost, it may stop moving.
issues.why: Bolts may be missing from the end cap of the stop/start accumulator on the transmission, letting fluid leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you see red fluid, have it towed rather than driven far.

issues.t: Crossover: tire sidewall or belt can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge in the sidewall, vibration, or a sudden blowout.
issues.why: Some original tires were over-cured at the factory, which can lead to sidewall breaks or tread belt separation.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and inspect the tires for bulges. Affected tires are replaced free.

issues.t: Crossover: roof-rail airbag inflator can come apart (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a crash, the side curtain airbag inflator could separate.
issues.why: A part of the roof-rail airbag inflator may separate during deployment, reducing protection and possibly injuring occupants.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the dealer replace the airbag.

issues.t: Crossover: seat belts held with the wrong bolts (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. A belt might not hold properly in a crash.
issues.why: Some seat belts were fastened with incorrect bolts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer installs the correct bolts.

issues.t: Crossover: driver seat frame weld may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The seat may not hold the driver properly in a crash.
issues.why: The driver's seat cushion frame may have a bad weld.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the seat frame is inspected and replaced if needed.

issues.t: Crossover: front axle shaft can come apart (recalls)
issues.sym: Clunking, loss of drive power, or the SUV rolling when in Park.
issues.why: On some 2023 models the left axle shaft may be missing a retaining ring, and others may have a wrong sun gear in the transmission, either of which can let an axle shaft disengage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and use the parking brake until the repair is done.

issues.t: Crossover: door strikers can break (recall)
issues.sym: A door may not stay latched, or may open while driving.
issues.why: Door strikers on some models were not heat-treated properly and can crack.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the strikers replaced free.

issues.t: Crossover: "Shift to Park" message and won't turn off
issues.sym: After shifting into Park, the dash says it isn't in Park and the vehicle won't shut off until you move the shifter several times.
issues.why: This is a widely reported shift-to-park problem on GM vehicles of this era, usually caused by a worn switch in the shifter.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about GM's shift-to-park repair; owners report paying for it out of warranty, so ask for a written quote.

issues.t: Crossover: several warning messages at once
issues.sym: Service engine, reduced power, service brake, reduced steering assist and StabiliTrak messages pop up together, sometimes with a slow start.
issues.why: GM traced some cases to vibration at the battery tray bracket and others to a weak battery or charging problem.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and ask about bulletin 23-NA-074.

issues.t: Crossover: starter grinds or spins without cranking
issues.sym: A grinding noise when starting, or the starter spins but the engine doesn't turn over.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover broken teeth on the flex plate (the toothed ring the starter turns) and starter problems.
issues.next: Have it checked soon; a damaged flex plate gets worse and can leave you stranded.

issues.t: Crossover: water leaks inside or liftgate acting up
issues.sym: Wet carpets or headliner, electrical glitches, or a noisy or inoperative power liftgate.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for water getting into the interior, which can also cause electrical problems and liftgate actuator trouble.
issues.next: Find and fix the leak quickly to prevent mold and electrical damage. Mention bulletin 19-NA-167.

issues.t: Crossover: check engine light from the crankcase pressure sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light, often with code P04FB, frequently in freezing weather.
issues.why: Moisture can freeze inside the crankcase pressure sensor and set a false code. On some 2025 models the sensor may not have been installed correctly at the factory.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the dealer about bulletins PIP5841 and PIP6055.

issues.t: Crossover: transmission case leak or clutch ring defect (GM programs)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid spots under the vehicle, or slipping and shift trouble.
issues.why: GM opened service programs for 2024 models: on some, the transmission case is porous near a mount bolt hole and leaks; on others, clutch retaining rings inside the transmission are out of spec.
issues.next: Ask a Chevrolet dealer to check your VIN for open programs N232433891 and N242446290; the repairs are done free.

issues.t: Crossover: front brake caliper bracket can crack (GM program)
issues.sym: Often no warning. A cracked bracket may cause noise, a pull or uneven braking.
issues.why: GM found that the front caliper bracket anchor on some 2024 models may crack, and dealers replace both brackets.
issues.next: Have a dealer check your VIN for program N242448390 and do the free repair.

issues.t: Crossover: "Service Safety Restraint" airbag warning
issues.sym: The airbag light comes on and the dash shows a Service Safety Restraint message.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for 2025 models showing this airbag system message.
issues.next: Have the airbag system checked soon; the airbags may not work while the light is on. Mention bulletin 25-NA-119.
